metadata.title: Primary and Secondary Raynaud: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association
top_takeaways: Raynaud phenomenon is classified into primary (PRP) and secondary (SRP) types, with SRP associated with underlying systemic conditions and a risk of severe digital ischemia or tissue loss.
Management of Raynaud phenomenon requires a combination of non-pharmacologic lifestyle modifications, targeted pharmacologic therapies, and treating any underlying systemic diseases.

Advanced imaging modalities can facilitate the earlier detection of secondary Raynaud phenomenon, and specialized interventions such as botulinum toxin therapy or surgery may be considered for severe cases.

recommendations.statement: Treating the underlying systemic disease is essential to improving vascular symptoms and preventing complications in patients with secondary Raynaud phenomenon (SRP).
recommendations.target_population: Patients with secondary Raynaud phenomenon (SRP) and underlying systemic conditions
